title: Early‐Stage Distribution of the Invasive Alga Rugulopteryx okamurae on the Catalan Coast: First Quantitative Baseline
content:
ABSTRACT

The non-indigenous brown alga Rugulopteryx okamurae has rapidly expanded across the eastern Atlantic and the western Mediterranean Sea. The first record on the Catalan coast (NW Mediterranean) was in July 2024 in Llançà (Girona), followed by additional detections at nearby localities. We conducted targeted surveys in June–July 2025 across 13 sampling stations in four localities, combining visual inspections and transects. R. okamurae was detected in nine out of 13 surveyed stations (69%). The species was most abundant on sheltered artificial substrates (inner ports, artificial pools), where mean cover reached 80%–85%, whereas natural rocky assemblages supported only sparse, patchy stands. These results establish the first quantitative baseline for Catalonia and support early monitoring and possible future management actions.
